note:
Paper 96, Team 42745, a space-debris removal and insurance model. Twenty-six pages, forty-three
measured regions on fifteen of them, resolving into TWENTY-FIVE FIGURE ROWS, THREE TABLE ROWS and
FIFTEEN EXCLUSIONS. Unaccounted zero. Ten of the exclusions are prose blocks the extractor boxed
because their text lines are drawn as paths, four are the image tiles that make up one figure, and
one is the references list.

The caption situation is the starkest in the lane so far. Twenty-four figures print a label and
eighteen of those are the bare form "Figure N" - no description, no unit, no condition, nothing.
Figure 1 appends a citation marker ("Figure 1 [12]"), Figure 6 appends a data-source credit
("Figure 6 (Data Source: Space-Track.org)"), and Figures 13 to 16 append the parameter their run
used ("Figure 13, 4%" through "Figure 16, logarithm"). Not one caption in the paper contains a word
describing its exhibit, which means the only identifying text is whatever MATLAB drew inside the
frame. The three tables carry no caption and no number at all: the notations table is introduced
only by "The following table provides meanings of important notations used in our models." and the
two payoff matrices are introduced by the two sentences that precede them.

One picture is printed nine times. The 1000 by 1000 debris matrix - grey grid, axes X and Y from 0
to 1000, a central void about 300 cells across, a dense ring at a radius of 700 to 800 cells, title
"Simulation Space Debris Distribution" inside the frame - appears as the executive summary's teaser
on p2, as Figure 5 at full size on p14, as Figures 8, 10 and 12 beside the profit charts at a
quarter of that size, and as Figures 13 to 16 at four increase rates on pp19-20. All nine boxes have
the same aspect, 1.117, at four different printed sizes. The four rate variants are distinguishable
only by the density of the point cloud and by the suffix on the caption; the in-plot title's
increase-rate clause is too small at printed size to read, and the axes carry cell indices with no
count, no total and no date anywhere.

Citation is close to absent. Only Figures 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 are named by a sentence, all five on the
two pages where they print - "Figure 1 shows the spatial density of debris in accordance with
altitude in LEO; Figure 3 is the three dimensional spread of debris, denoted by black dots, in LEO",
"shown in figure 2" in the lower case, "and derive Figure 4", and "can be vividly shown in the
following Figure 5, Figure 5" where the pointer's own trailing label collides with the printed one.
Figures 6 to 24 are pointed at only by phrases that name nothing: "the results are presented in the
following figures", "present the corresponding figures", "The figures presented above are also
developed by using the combined alternative". A reader who wants to know which of the eight
identical profit charts is the 9-year run has to read the title inside the frame.

Two exhibits contradict the sentences beside them. Figure 6 prints the observed launch catalogue -
markers falling from 115 to 40 and climbing back to 150 between 2001 and 2015, with a dotted trend
line that no legend keys - while the text says the model starts at 110 satellites and "will increase
by 5% each year"; a monotone 5% growth is not what the picture shows, and the dotted trend matches
neither. Figure 7 and its three twins carry the title "The Profits v.s. the Number of Debris
remaining" over a right axis labelled "Debris left", name the same series two different ways, and
print no unit on that axis at all. Both defects are in what the exhibit says, not in how it is
drawn.

Design. The two payoff matrices on p23 are 4 by 4 grids with a single vertical rule between the stub
column and the payoff cells and a single rule under the header - no box, no interior lines - and
their read-out depends entirely on underlining: two cells are underlined in the first matrix, which
are exactly the two Nash equilibria the prose names, and one cell is underlined in the second, which
is the single equilibrium the new standards are claimed to produce. No line of text explains the
convention, and neither matrix prints a unit, so the pairs are billions of profit and of
compensation only if the reader carries that over from the axes of Figures 7 to 12. The notations
table on p8 rules every body row and closes no box.

Families: bar 11, scatter 10, line 2, histogram 1, heatmap-or-contour 1, table-grid 3.
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: forty-three measured regions resolve into twenty-five figure rows, three table rows and fifteen exclusions, and no region is counted twice [place.doc_order].

The caption is a number and nothing else: twenty-four figures print a label and eighteen of them print the bare form 'Figure N', while Figure 1 appends a citation marker, Figure 6 a data-source credit and Figures 13 to 16 the parameter their run used - so no row's caption block is built out of anything but what prints below the exhibit [caption.words].

The plotting program's title is not a caption: nine rows print 'Simulation Space Debris Distribution' inside their own frame and eight print '_lifetime_N' or '_alpha_N%' there, and every one of those titles is carried in the note and in the geometry instead of being promoted to a caption [caption.verbatim].

A bare pointer is not a citation: 'the results are presented in the following figures', 'present the corresponding figures' and 'The figures presented above are also developed by using the combined alternative' name no exhibit, so twenty figure rows and all three tables record no citation at all [mention.count].

An abstract can print an exhibit: the teaser on p2 is recorded as its own row with no caption and no citation because the same plot is printed again as Figure 5, and both printings are measured regions [place.page_zone].

A region inside a region is a fragment of the exhibit, not a second exhibit: the four image tiles measured inside Figure 4's frame are exclusions, and the nine prose blocks on pp6-7 and the references block on p25 are exclusions because they carry no picture [place.area_frac].

Placement follows the heading index, which indexed every heading this paper prints including the one whose label carries mathematics; p20 prints two figures at its very top and the '7.2 Scenario 2' heading at its foot, so those two rows belong to 7.1 [place.section_path].

A caption suffix that names a parameter stays in the caption: 'Figure 13, 4%' keeps the 4%, because the increase rate is the only thing that distinguishes the four point clouds of pp19-20 from one another [caption.numbering].

tables.note: The paper's only table of definitions: two columns headed 'Symbols' and 'Meanings' and fifteen body rows - N_t net income, R_t revenue from insurance, C_t total cost, NT cumulative net income, n_t satellites launched, w the guaranteed amount, alpha the actuarial constant, C1_t and C2_t the two cost terms, p_t price, q_t quantity trapped, Pr(t) the collision chance, delta the compensating parameter, Q_t debris in space, epsilon the removal per trapper. Ruling: heavy rules above the header, under it and at the foot, a thin rule between EVERY body row, and one full-height vertical rule between the two columns - no outer box and no side strokes beyond that single interior vertical. The Symbols column is centred italic mathematics. NO CAPTION AND NO NUMBER: the table is introduced only by 'The following table provides meanings of important notations used in our models.', and only the last cell's meaning ends with a full stop.

The game's payoff matrix as a 4 by 4 grid: a stub column headed 'Player1/2', three column heads ('Do nothing', 'Remove some', 'Remove considerably') and three row stubs ('Uninsured', 'Half insured', 'Fully insured'), with nine cells each holding a pair like '(-45,0)'. Ruling: one vertical rule between the stub column and the payoff columns and one horizontal rule under the header row, and nothing else - no top rule, no foot rule, no box, no interior lines, no zebra. THE TWO NASH EQUILIBRIA THE PROSE NAMES ARE MARKED ONLY BY UNDERLINING: '(-21,-8.4)' at (half insured, remove considerably) and '(-27,-11.7)' at (fully insured, remove some) are underlined, and not one line of text says what an underline means. No unit is printed anywhere in either matrix - the pairs are billions of profit and of compensation, which the reader carries over from the axes of Figures 7 to 12 - and no caption or number stands above or below it.

The same matrix recomputed as the paper's new payoff matrix after the proposed standards: identical 4 by 4 structure, ruling and cell style as the matrix above, with different values in every cell, and exactly ONE cell underlined, '(-19.5,-3.3)' at (half insured, remove considerably) - the single Nash equilibrium the prose claims the new standards shift the game to. The pair of matrices is the only exhibit pair in the paper whose read-out is a marking convention rather than a shape, and the convention is never stated. Both matrices repeat the same stub header 'Player1/2' without ever saying who player 1 and player 2 are; the prose has to be read to learn that they are the launch operator and the insurance provider.
